title: Named in Congress (2015)
hookLine: Pope Francis names Merton among four great Americans

cards: The United States Capitol, September 24, 2015. The chamber of the House of Representatives is packed: senators, representatives, justices, cameras.
For the first time in history, a pope stands at the podium to address Congress. Pope Francis speaks in English, slowly, about immigrants, the poor, the death penalty, and the earth.

And to hold it all together, he tells the story of four Americans. Three are a president, a preacher and a journalist who fed the hungry. The fourth is a monk who'd spent most of his adult life in silence.

teach.b: First, the four. Francis named Abraham Lincoln, for liberty. Martin Luther King Jr., for his dream of rights for all.
Dorothy Day, the Catholic journalist who co-founded the Catholic Worker and spent her life serving the poor. And Thomas Merton. Second, what he said about Merton.
Francis called him a man of dialogue and a promoter of peace between peoples and religions.
Above all, he said, Merton was a man of prayer, a thinker who challenged the certainties of his time and opened new horizons for souls and for the Church.

teach.h: A MAN OF DIALOGUE AND PRAYER.
teach.b: Prayer, dialogue, peace, challenge: every stretch of Merton's road in these weeks. Third, why it was a surprise.
For years, some Catholics had been uneasy about Merton: his outspokenness about war, his friendships across traditions, his restless questions.
To hear a pope name him in front of Congress, beside Lincoln and King, told his readers that his questions had a home in the Church. Fourth, remembering as a Catholic act.
At the Last Supper, Jesus said, in the Douay-Rheims: "Do this for a commemoration of me."
For Catholics, remembering isn't just nostalgia: it keeps a person's gift alive and working in the present.

teach.h: DO THIS FOR A COMMEMORATION OF ME.
teach.b: The Church remembers its saints on their feast days. Merton isn't a canonized saint, but a pope chose to remember him out loud.
A monk who ran from fame was held up for a whole nation, because of what his hidden life had given.

how: Catholics remember holy men and women in the Church's calendar of saints and in prayers for the dead, and many honor teachers like Merton and Dorothy Day by reading their work and continuing it.

o: a remembering that makes someone present again
a sad longing for the good old days, long gone
a forgetting of past wrongs, for the sake of peace

p: a dream of rights for all
the Catholic Worker and the poor

s: Pope Francis was the first pope to address Congress
Merton has been canonized a saint
he isn't a canonized saint; the pope held him up as a great American and a man of prayer.
Francis called Merton a man of dialogue
a promoter of peace between peoples and religions, and above all a man of prayer.

games.q: you're the pope, speaking to Congress about the poor, immigrants and peace. which four Americans do you name?
o: Lincoln, King, Dorothy Day and Thomas Merton
four saints of the early Church
games.why: Francis named Lincoln, King, Dorothy Day and Merton, and called Merton a man of prayer who opened new horizons.

practice: Look around for one thing that carries a person in it, a song you hum, a phrase you repeat, a book on the shelf, the way you fold a shirt, and follow it back to whoever gave it to you: a grandparent, a teacher, a coach, an author you never met.
Say their name quietly, name the gift in a few words, and stay grateful for a moment. If you pray, you can thank God for them, living or dead.

wordCard.voice: Anamnesis, the Greek word behind Jesus's 'do this for a commemoration of me': a remembering that makes the person present again. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: remembrance, the word behind 'do this for a commemoration of me', memory that makes present.

carryVoice: Your line: a monk remembered. His questions had a home. Day two hundred eighty-eight.

sources.q: Do this for a commemoration of me.
